question: Outline, with dated and quantified evidence, the impact of the 1929 crash on unemployment in Germany between 1929 and 1932. Write no more than 200 words and give a judgement on which year marked the turning point.
response_text: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 led American lenders to recall the short-term credit on which the Weimar economy depended, and registered unemployment then rose in each year that followed. Annual averages climbed from about 1.9 million in 1929 to 3.1 million in 1930, 4.5 million in 1931 and 5.6 million in 1932, peaking at about 6.1 million in February 1932 (figures from memory; check them against your notes). Brüning's deflationary decrees of December 1930 and June 1931 cut wages and benefits and deepened the fall in demand, while the collapse of the Danatbank on 13 July 1931 turned the slump into a banking crisis. The turning point was 1930. The annual average grew by roughly 60 per cent that year, the greatest proportional rise of the period, and the increase became a sustained mass crisis rather than a cyclical dip, which fed the political break of the September 1930 election. The strongest counter-case is 1932, the peak year, but a peak within a rising trend marks the height of the crisis rather than the point at which its direction changed, so by the criterion of when the trajectory altered it weighs less.
